title: Ask an AI tool
notice_desktop: This page is for a computer screen. It is not made for phones.
intro: Copy a ready-made prompt, paste it into an AI tool, then import the file it makes. You do not need an account here. The tools below may.

evidence_key.F: Read on the tool's own page on the check date.
evidence_key.S: Read in a search summary only. Check it before you rely on it.
evidence_key.G: From general knowledge, not checked. Check it.
evidence_key.mixed: Part read on the tool's own page, part from general knowledge.

terms_note: Terms change. Read the tool's own terms before you use what it makes.

guide.title: Ask for one clear subject
guide.text: Say one thing: a harbour at dusk, or paper shapes sliding in. Two ideas in one prompt give a muddle.

guide.title: Add style words
guide.text: Words such as flat, cinematic, retro, paper cut-out or soft focus change the result more than anything else. Pick one style, not three.

guide.title: Say the length
guide.text: Give the length in seconds. Most free video tools make 5 or 10 seconds. If you need longer, make several and join them.

guide.title: Say the shape and size
guide.text: Say 16:9 and 1920 by 1080. If the tool offers a shape menu, choose 16:9 there too, as the menu often wins over the words.

guide.title: Leave words out
guide.text: AI tools often spell words wrongly or change them between frames. Ask for no words, then add the channel name in the plug-in.

guide.title: Keep people and brands out
guide.text: Ask for no real people, no real logos and no brand names. Do not ask for the style of a living artist, or for a famous song.

guide.title: Ask for calm, clear results
guide.text: Ask for no flashing. Ask for plain areas where words will go. Ask for music with an even level and no singing.

guide.title: Try three times, then change one thing
guide.text: The first result is rarely the best. Change one word at a time, so you learn what each word does.

guide.title: Keep a record and add credits
guide.text: Write down the tool, the date, the plan (free or paid) and the prompt. Put it in a file named LICENCE.txt in your kit, with the credit line for each file.

sources.name: Microsoft Image Creator (Bing)
sources.free_tier: Free with a personal Microsoft account.
sources.limits: 15 fast creations a day that refill each day. After that, slower creations, up to 200 prompts in 24 hours. The page also says 10 in one place, so the number is not steady.
sources.watermark: A visible watermark by default. A signed-in person can turn it off in Settings.
sources.resolution: Not stated on the page I read.
sources.use_terms: The help page does not say whether use is personal or commercial. It points to the Image Creator Terms, which I did not read. One search summary says personal use only.
sources.sign_in: A personal Microsoft account. Work or school accounts cannot use it.
sources.notes: Read the Image Creator Terms before you use a picture in public.

sources.name: Adobe Firefly
sources.makes: Pictures and short video from a prompt.
sources.free_tier: A free plan with limited free daily generations for images and video.
sources.limits: Limited. One generation at a time. The page gives no numbers.
sources.watermark: Not stated on the page I read.
sources.resolution: Not stated on the page I read.
sources.use_terms: Adobe says output from its own Firefly models can be used commercially. Pictures made with partner models may have other terms, so check each one.
sources.notes: The free plan page does not say whether pictures carry a watermark or a content mark. Check the first result.

sources.name: Ideogram
sources.free_tier: Read this carefully: on 28 November 2026 the help page says new accounts without a creator badge get no free credits.
sources.limits: Older eligible accounts keep 30 credits a week. Free credits reset on Saturdays.
sources.watermark: Reports disagree and the page does not say.
sources.resolution: Not stated on the page I read.
sources.use_terms: Pictures made with free credits are public. Whether free use may be commercial is not clear: reports disagree, and the page points to the Terms of Service.
sources.sign_in: An account. Sign-in by Google, Apple, Microsoft or email does not by itself bring free credits.
sources.notes: Probably not a free choice for a new account. Left in so you know why it is not recommended.

sources.name: Leonardo.ai
sources.makes: Pictures and some video from a prompt.
sources.free_tier: A free plan with a daily allowance of tokens.
sources.limits: Reports say 150 tokens a day that do not carry over. Not confirmed: the official page refused to load.
sources.use_terms: Reports disagree on commercial use. Reports say free-plan pictures are visible to other people on the site.
sources.notes: I could not read Leonardo's own terms. Read them first.

sources.name: Craiyon
sources.limits: Slower on the free plan. Exact limits not confirmed.
sources.watermark: A small Craiyon watermark on free pictures (reported).
sources.use_terms: Reported: free commercial use needs a credit to Craiyon. A business with more than 1 million US dollars a year needs a separate licence. Free pictures may be public. The official terms page refused to load.
sources.sign_in: None needed for the free use (reported).
sources.notes: A good first try because there is no account. Quality is lower than the others.

sources.name: Google Gemini (the app and site)
sources.makes: Pictures from a prompt, and short video on paid plans.
sources.limits: A daily limit that Google changes often. Reports range from about 20 to 100 pictures a day. Video is on paid plans, except a small daily credit allowance in Flow (reported).
sources.use_terms: Not read. Read Google's terms for generative tools.
sources.notes: Google's own limits page is: support.google.com/gemini/answer/16275805. I did not read it.

sources.name: Perchance image generators
sources.makes: Pictures from a prompt, from community-made generators.
sources.free_tier: Free and, by report, without a sign-in or a daily cap.
sources.limits: No cap reported. The pages can be slow and may show advertisements.
sources.use_terms: Not found. Reports say commercial rights depend on the generator and on the model behind it.
sources.notes: Each generator on Perchance is made by a different person. There is no download button on some, so you may have to save the picture by right-click.

sources.name: Runway
sources.makes: Short video from a prompt or a picture.
sources.free_tier: 125 credits once, not each month. They do not run out with time.
sources.limits: Not stated what 125 credits make. A few clips at most.
sources.watermark: Not stated for the free plan. The page lists No watermarks as a paid feature.
sources.use_terms: Commercial use is not mentioned for the free plan.
sources.notes: Enough to try it, not enough to run a channel.

sources.name: Luma Dream Machine
sources.makes: Short video from a prompt or a picture.
sources.free_tier: A free plan exists. The pricing page says it differs from paid plans in credits, watermark, resolution and commercial use, but gives no numbers.
sources.watermark: The page says there is a difference. Details not stated.
sources.resolution: The page says there is a difference. Details not stated.
sources.use_terms: Paid plans, from 30 US dollars a month, include commercial use. The free plan does not, by the page's own comparison.
sources.notes: Check the free numbers on the site before you spend time on it.

sources.name: Pika
sources.makes: Short video from a prompt or a picture.
sources.free_tier: Not a free choice as I read it: the Free plan has no monthly credits. Credits are bought in packs.
sources.watermark: The pricing page says Free exports have no watermark.
sources.resolution: Not stated on the page I read.
sources.use_terms: The comparison table says the commercial licence is No for the Free plan.
sources.notes: Left in so you know why it is not recommended.

sources.name: Kling AI
sources.makes: Short video from a prompt or a picture.
sources.free_tier: Not confirmed. The pricing page I opened showed no plan details.
sources.notes: Listed only so you can check it yourself.

sources.name: Suno
sources.makes: Songs and instrumental tracks from a prompt.
sources.free_tier: Free plan: 50 credits a day, which do not carry over.
sources.limits: Up to 4 songs at once. The pricing page says the free plan has no monthly song downloads, so check you can save the file before you plan around it.
sources.use_terms: Commercial rights are not included on the free plan (Pro and above include them). Personal use at home is what this channel is.
sources.notes: Ask for instrumental, with no singing.

sources.name: Udio
sources.makes: Songs and instrumental tracks from a prompt.
sources.free_tier: A free plan with a small daily and monthly allowance (reported: 10 a day, 100 a month).
sources.limits: Reported: a cap on longer tracks each day. Credits do not roll over.
sources.use_terms: Reports disagree. Several 2026 reports say free output is for personal, non-commercial use and that downloads may be blocked. I did not read Udio's own terms.
sources.notes: Check on the site that downloads are allowed before you use it.

sources.name: Stable Audio (the website)
sources.makes: Music and sound effects from a prompt.
sources.limits: The page I read gave no numbers.
sources.use_terms: The page says the licence depends on the plan. No details.
sources.notes: The open model behind it, Stable Audio Open, is in the list of programs you can run yourself.

sources.name: MusicGen demo on Hugging Face
sources.makes: Short music clips from a prompt.
sources.free_tier: Free to try in the browser. Demos can have a queue.
sources.use_terms: The model files are licensed Creative Commons BY-NC 4.0: non-commercial. That suits a home channel but not selling. A Space can be taken down.
sources.notes: Licence read on the model's own page. The demo's limits are from general knowledge.

sources.name: TTSMaker
sources.makes: Spoken audio from typed text, in many voices and languages.
sources.free_tier: Free. A site page says 20,000 characters a week, with some voices unlimited.
sources.limits: Files are kept for a short time (reported 30 minutes), so download straight away.
sources.use_terms: The site says commercial use is allowed for free, but its terms add conditions for some features. I read only the first part.
sources.notes: Read the Terms of Service page for your voice.

sources.name: ElevenLabs
sources.limits: Credits run out quickly for long text.
sources.use_terms: The commercial licence is a paid add-on from the Starter plan. The page does not say what Free allows. It does not mention a credit rule.
sources.notes: Use it for one or two lines, not for long reading.

sources.name: A logo from a picture tool, then clean up
sources.makes: A simple shape that you clean up yourself.
sources.free_tier: Use any picture tool above, then trace the result in Inkscape (free, open source) or remove the background in GIMP or Krita.
sources.resolution: Trace to a vector so it stays sharp at any size.
sources.use_terms: Follow the picture tool's terms. Inkscape, GIMP and Krita are free software and put no limits on what you make.
sources.notes: Logo makers such as Looka let you design for free but charge to download, so they are left out.

local_sources.name: Stable Diffusion XL, with ComfyUI or stable-diffusion.cpp
local_sources.free_tier: Free. No sign-in, no limits, nothing leaves your computer.
local_sources.use_terms: SDXL 1.0 uses the CreativeML OpenRAIL++-M licence (read on the model page). ComfyUI is GPL-3.0 and stable-diffusion.cpp is MIT (read on GitHub). Stable Diffusion 3.5 uses the Stability AI Community Licence, free below an income limit (read on the model page; I did not read the limit).
local_sources.notes: Pick a model whose licence you have read.
local_sources.hardware: A computer with a graphics card with about 8 GB of video memory is comfortable (general knowledge, not measured). Without a graphics card it works on the processor but takes minutes for each picture. Do not run it on the Starboard server.

local_sources.name: FLUX.1 schnell
local_sources.makes: Fast, good pictures on your own computer.
local_sources.free_tier: Free. No sign-in for the model files (Hugging Face may ask you to accept a licence for some models).
local_sources.resolution: Up to about 1024 by 1024 or more.
local_sources.notes: A good default for stills, with ComfyUI or diffusers.
local_sources.hardware: A large model (12 billion settings). A graphics card with 12 to 24 GB works best, smaller with compressed versions (general knowledge). Not for a small server.

local_sources.name: Stable Video Diffusion
local_sources.makes: A short moving clip from a still picture.
local_sources.free_tier: Free to run. No sign-in for the files I read, apart from accepting the licence.
local_sources.use_terms: Stability AI's own Stable Video Diffusion community licence (read the name on the model page, not the text).
local_sources.notes: Older and smaller than the newer models. Useful for making a still picture move gently.
local_sources.hardware: Needs a graphics card with plenty of video memory, around 16 GB or more for the longer version (general knowledge, not measured).

local_sources.name: LTX-Video
local_sources.makes: Short video from text or a picture, on your own computer.
local_sources.resolution: Up to 1216 by 704 and more with newer versions (general knowledge).
local_sources.use_terms: The code is Apache-2.0 (read on GitHub). The model files use the LTX-Video open-weights licence (read the name on the model page, not the text): read it.
local_sources.notes: The project describes a smaller 2 billion model for light video memory use.
local_sources.hardware: A graphics card with 8 to 12 GB for the small model, 24 GB or more for the large one (general knowledge). Not for a small server.

local_sources.name: Wan 2.1 and 2.2
local_sources.makes: Short video from text or a picture, on your own computer.
local_sources.use_terms: Apache-2.0 for code and for the model files I checked (read on GitHub and the model page).
local_sources.notes: Good results for a free model. The 1.3 billion and 5 billion versions are the small ones.
local_sources.hardware: The 1.3 billion version is reported to run on about 8 GB of video memory, the 5 billion version on a 24 GB card (general knowledge, not measured). A few minutes for a 5 second clip on a good card. Not for a small server.

local_sources.name: MusicGen (AudioCraft)
local_sources.makes: Instrumental music from a prompt, on your own computer.
local_sources.limits: Clips of about 30 seconds at a time (general knowledge).
local_sources.use_terms: The code is MIT (read on GitHub). The model files I checked are Creative Commons BY-NC 4.0: non-commercial (read on the model page). Fine for a home channel.
local_sources.notes: Small models can run on a processor, slowly.
local_sources.hardware: The small model runs on a processor; a graphics card makes it much faster (general knowledge, not measured).
local_sources.licence: MIT code; CC BY-NC 4.0 model files

local_sources.name: Stable Audio Open
local_sources.makes: Short music and sound effects from a prompt.
local_sources.free_tier: Free to run. You must agree to the licence on Hugging Face first, which needs a free account to download.
local_sources.use_terms: Stability AI community licences (read the names on the model pages, not the text). The tools code (stable-audio-tools) is MIT.
local_sources.sign_in: A free Hugging Face account to download the model files.
local_sources.notes: The one local choice here that asks for an account, only to download the file once.
local_sources.hardware: The small version is made to run on modest hardware, even a phone (general knowledge). Not measured.

local_sources.name: Piper (text to speech)
local_sources.makes: Spoken audio from text, on your own computer.
local_sources.use_terms: The original Piper (MIT) was archived in August 2025. Its successor is GPL-3.0 (read on GitHub). Each voice has its own licence: read the card of the voice you use.
local_sources.notes: Many voices in many languages. Works on a processor.
local_sources.hardware: Fast on an ordinary processor, even a small computer (general knowledge, not measured here).

local_sources.name: Kokoro (text to speech)
local_sources.makes: Natural-sounding speech on your own computer.
local_sources.notes: A small model of 82 million settings.
local_sources.hardware: Runs on a processor (general knowledge, not measured).

local_sources.name: Coqui TTS and XTTS
local_sources.use_terms: The code is MPL-2.0 (read on GitHub). The XTTS-v2 model files use the Coqui Public Model Licence, which is non-commercial (read the name on the model page). Do not clone a real person's voice.
local_sources.notes: The company behind it closed in early 2024 (general knowledge). The code lives on in a fork.
local_sources.hardware: Runs on a processor slowly and on a graphics card well (general knowledge).

safety.title: Terms change
safety.text: Free plans, limits and rules change often. The notes here were checked on 28 November 2026. Read the tool's own terms before you use anything it makes.

safety.title: Home use is the safe side
safety.text: Most free plans allow personal use and many do not allow commercial use. A channel at home, for your family, is personal use. Do not sell or share it for money.

safety.title: Free pictures may be public
safety.text: Some tools show what you make to other people. Never type private things, names of children, addresses or passwords into a prompt.

safety.title: No real people and no brands
safety.text: Do not ask for a real person, a famous character, a real logo, a brand or a real song. The result may copy them, and you would not own that.

safety.title: Keep credits
safety.text: Put the tool name, the date, the plan and your prompt in a file named LICENCE.txt in your kit. You do not need an AI label on the channel.

safety.title: Check before you import
safety.text: Play each file once. Check for flashing, odd words, a watermark in a corner, and a loud start. A watermark means the free plan wants a credit or a paid plan.

safety.title: Your own accounts and details
safety.text: Making an account is your own choice. Never give an AI tool your Starboard address, keys or passwords. The tools do not need them.

safety.title: Open-source tools on your own computer
safety.text: They send nothing out and have no limits, but they need a computer with a graphics card for video. Do not run them on the Starboard server.
